units.title: Essential Greetings & Daily Life
units.description: Master polite introductions, common phrases, and everyday conversational English.

questions.prompt: Select the most polite way to introduce yourself to a new colleague:
options: Hello, nice to meet you! I am Alex.
questions.explanation: "Hello, nice to meet you!" is warm, professional, and courteous.

questions.prompt: Complete the sentence with the correct greeting:
questions.sentence: Good ___, sir! Welcome to the Grand Central Hotel.
questions.explanation: "Good morning" is the conventional formal greeting used before noon.

questions.prompt: Assemble the sentence in the correct natural order:
questions.explanation: Standard polite greeting structure: "Nice to meet you [Name]".

questions.prompt: Match each English greeting with its appropriate response:
questions.explanation: These are customary conversational pairings in everyday English.

questions.prompt: Listen carefully to the audio and select what you heard:
questions.explanation: "Where are you from?" inquires about nationality or origin.

questions.prompt: Read the greeting aloud clearly:
questions.targetText: I am pleased to meet you today.
questions.phoneticHint: eye am pleezd too meet yoo tuh-day
questions.explanation: Ensure clear pronunciation of "pleased" (/pliːzd/).

questions.prompt: Which response is most suitable when someone says "Thank you very much"?
questions.explanation: "You're very welcome!" is the standard courteous reply.

questions.prompt: Fill in the missing word:
questions.sentence: My ___ is David and I am an architect.
questions.explanation: "My name is..." is used to declare your identity.

questions.prompt: What is the polite phrase to order a hot beverage?
options: Could I have a cappuccino, please?
questions.explanation: "Could I have..., please?" is the ideal polite customer request.

questions.prompt: Arrange the words to ask for the bill:
questions.correctSentence: Can we have the bill please
questions.explanation: "Can we have the bill, please?" asks the waiter for the check.

questions.prompt: Complete the barista's question:
questions.sentence: Would you like that for ___ or to go?
questions.explanation: "For here or to go?" asks whether you will consume in the café or take away.

questions.prompt: Match the café term with its meaning:
questions.explanation: Key café and restaurant transaction vocabulary.

questions.prompt: Listen to the customer's order:
questions.audioText: An iced latte with oat milk, please.
options: An iced latte with oat milk, please.
A hot latte with almond milk, please.
An iced tea with lemon juice, please.
A green tea with honey, please.
questions.explanation: Clear order specification with beverage type and milk preference.

questions.prompt: Speak this sentence into the microphone:
questions.targetText: Could I get a glass of water?
questions.phoneticHint: kood eye get uh glas ov wah-ter
questions.explanation: Use a gentle rising intonation for polite questions.

questions.prompt: What does a barista mean by "Any pastries with that?"
options: Do you want something sweet or baked to eat?
Do you have a loyalty card?
Where would you like to sit?
questions.explanation: Pastries include croissants, muffins, scones, and danishes.

questions.prompt: Fill in the blank with the correct preposition:
questions.sentence: I take my coffee ___ sugar and a splash of milk.
questions.explanation: Use "with" to indicate ingredients added to food/drinks.

questions.prompt: How do you politely ask a stranger for directions?
options: Excuse me, could you tell me where the library is?
questions.explanation: "Excuse me, could you tell me..." softens an unsolicited question to a stranger.

questions.prompt: Build the direction phrase:
questions.correctSentence: Turn left at the traffic lights
questions.explanation: Standard imperative instruction for vehicle or walking navigation.

questions.prompt: Choose the correct preposition of place:
questions.sentence: The bank is directly ___ the museum on Oxford Street.
questions.explanation: "Opposite" means on the other side of the road facing it.

questions.prompt: Match each navigation phrase to its meaning:
questions.explanation: Common directional spatial markers.

questions.prompt: Listen carefully to the commuter's instruction:
questions.audioText: Take the subway two stops to Central Park.
options: Take the subway two stops to Central Park.
Take the bus three stops to Central Station.
Walk two blocks toward Central Park.
Take the taxi directly to the park.
questions.explanation: Listening for mode of transport and destination.

questions.prompt: Pronounce this sentence clearly:
questions.targetText: Is the train station within walking distance?
questions.phoneticHint: iz thuh trayn stay-shun with-in wahk-ing dis-tuns
questions.explanation: "Walking distance" refers to a short journey you can walk on foot.

questions.prompt: If a landmark is "two blocks away", what does that mean?
options: It is approximately two street intersections away.
It is closed for two weeks.
It has two large concrete blocks.
It is two hours by train.
questions.explanation: A "block" is the distance along a street from one cross-street to the next.

questions.prompt: Fill in the blank with the appropriate word:
questions.sentence: You cannot miss it; it is right on your ___ hand side.
questions.explanation: "On your right/left hand side" is common directional parlance.

units.title: Travel, Work & Everyday Life
units.description: Expand into airport travel, workplace emails, and weekend leisure plans.

questions.prompt: What document must you present when boarding an aircraft?
questions.explanation: A boarding pass and valid passport are mandatory for boarding flights.

questions.prompt: Complete the airport security instruction:
questions.sentence: Please place all liquids into a clear ___ bag.
questions.explanation: Airport security regulations stipulate transparent plastic bags for liquids.

questions.prompt: Arrange into a flight attendant announcement:
questions.correctSentence: Please fasten your seatbelts for takeoff
questions.explanation: Crucial aviation safety instruction during taxi and takeoff.

questions.prompt: Match each airport terminal sign to its meaning:
questions.explanation: Essential terminal navigation vocabulary.

questions.prompt: Listen to the gate agent's announcement:
questions.audioText: Flight 204 to London is now boarding at Gate 14.
options: Flight 204 to London is now boarding at Gate 14.
Flight 204 to Paris is delayed until 4 PM.
Flight 402 to London is arriving at Gate 40.
Flight 214 to New York has changed gates.
questions.explanation: Focus on the flight number (204) and gate number (14).

questions.prompt: Read this check-in query clearly:
questions.targetText: I would prefer a window seat if possible.
questions.phoneticHint: eye wood pree-fer uh win-doh seet if pos-uh-bul
questions.explanation: Practice stating personal seating preferences politely.

questions.prompt: What is the difference between "carry-on" and "checked baggage"?
options: Carry-on stays with you in the cabin; checked goes in the cargo hold.
Carry-on is sent by mail; checked baggage is held by customs.
Both mean bags that weigh over 50 kilograms.
Carry-on is only for duty-free items.
questions.explanation: Cabin luggage vs cargo luggage is a vital travel distinction.

questions.prompt: Fill in the blank with the correct travel verb:
questions.sentence: Our flight was ___ by two hours due to heavy fog.
questions.explanation: Flights are delayed when their departure is postponed.

questions.prompt: Choose the most professional opening for an email to a new client:
questions.explanation: "Dear Mr. [Last Name]" is the standard formal greeting in business communication.

questions.prompt: Form a polite sentence referencing an attachment:
questions.correctSentence: Please find attached the quarterly report
questions.explanation: "Please find attached..." is the standard business formula for files sent.

questions.prompt: Complete the polite scheduling sentence:
questions.sentence: Please let me know if Tuesday at 10 AM is ___ for you.
questions.explanation: "Convenient" means suitable for someone's schedule or comfort.

questions.prompt: Match the email closing with its level of formality:
questions.explanation: Selecting the right sign-off demonstrates cultural and situational awareness.

questions.prompt: Listen to the executive's voicemail message:
questions.audioText: I look forward to discussing the project tomorrow.
options: I look forward to discussing the project tomorrow.
I forgot about our project meeting yesterday.
I would like to cancel the contract immediately.
Let us delay the project until next quarter.
questions.explanation: "Look forward to + gerund" indicates eager anticipation.

questions.prompt: Practice saying this professional sentence aloud:
questions.targetText: Thank you for your prompt response to my email.
questions.phoneticHint: thank yoo for yoor prompt ree-spons too my ee-mayl
questions.explanation: "Prompt" in this context means swift, quick, and timely.

questions.prompt: What does the abbreviation "FYI" in a work email mean?
questions.explanation: FYI is a common workplace acronym meaning no immediate action is required.

questions.prompt: Fill in the blank with the correct preposition:
questions.sentence: I will get back to you ___ the end of the day.
questions.explanation: "By the end of the day" denotes a deadline before or at close of business.

questions.prompt: Select the correct sentence expressing a future plan:
options: I am going to visit the modern art gallery on Saturday.
I will visiting the gallery last week.
questions.explanation: "be going to + verb" is naturally used for planned future intentions.

questions.prompt: Build an invitation for a friend:
questions.correctSentence: Do you want to grab lunch together
questions.explanation: "To grab lunch" is an informal, friendly idiom for having a meal.

questions.prompt: Complete the hobby description:
questions.sentence: In my spare time, I really enjoy ___ photos of nature.
questions.explanation: We say "take photos" or "taking photographs" in English.

questions.prompt: Match each leisure activity with its fitting collocated verb:
questions.explanation: English verbs for sports: 'go' (-ing), 'play' (ball/team sports), 'do' (martial arts/activities).

questions.prompt: Listen to the weekend suggestion:
questions.audioText: How about going for a hike in the mountains?
options: How about going for a hike in the mountains?
We must clean the house this weekend.
The mountains are too cold for camping.
Have you ever climbed Mount Everest?
questions.explanation: "How about + verb-ing" is a common structure for friendly suggestions.

questions.prompt: Say this conversational sentence out loud:
questions.targetText: That sounds like a wonderful idea!
questions.phoneticHint: that sowndz lyk uh wun-der-ful eye-dee-uh
questions.explanation: Express genuine enthusiasm when accepting invitations.

questions.prompt: What does someone mean when they say "I'll take a rain check"?
options: They decline now but want to reschedule for another time.
They are looking at the weather forecast.
They want you to pay with cash.
questions.explanation: "Take a rain check" politely declines an offer now with promise to accept later.

questions.prompt: Fill in the blank with the correct adverb:
questions.sentence: The concert was ___ sold out within minutes.
questions.explanation: "Completely sold out" indicates that all tickets were bought.
